learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparing numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected Water 5 units, buffer 5 and locked it in. Intro defines pH factor of ten and buffer resistance before prediction.
observations.exploration: Added first 0.001 mol dose: water 7.00 to 3.00, buffer 4.76 to 4.75, acetate 0.099/acetic acid 0.101. Add the rest ran sequentially to ten doses: water 2.00, buffer 4.67, acetate 0.090/acetic acid 0.110.
observations.reveal: Not quite identifies water five units, buffer under 0.1. Explains free hydrogen ions, acetate becoming acetic acid, changing ratio and blood pH 7.4.
observations.visual: Inline initial and completed screenshots inspected. White water curve plunges first dose; pink buffer curve nearly flat. Initial numeric badges partly clipped within stage; completed stage badges visible. Reveal text in same stage requires scrolling.
observations.isolation: No-history evaluation preview banner present. 7/7 trust counter ignored.
references: CUA tab 543884107 snapshots and inline screenshots; no screenshot file saved.

prediction.reason: Numerical alternatives are clear, but definition that buffer resists pH changes cues intended qualitative answer.
prediction.evidence: Prediction prompt explicitly defines buffer before alternatives.

interaction.reason: Dose sequence makes first-dose water plunge and buffer resistance visibly contrast.
interaction.evidence: First dose and final tenth dose numbers, plotted curves.

payoff.reason: Connects observed quantities to ion capture and acetate ratio.

clarity.reason: Core path usable, but initial numeric badges partly clipped and chemistry-heavy prompt raises reading burden.
clarity.evidence: Initial screenshot clipped badge row; completed chart legible.

transfer.reason: Blood offered as new example without conditions or a fresh task.
transfer.evidence: Blood is buffered too, near pH 7.4.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard, focus, contrast audit, phone, zoom/reflow and motion unknown.

surprise.reason: Committed equal-drop prediction contradicted by sharply different outcomes.
surprise.evidence: Five-unit water drop versus under 0.1 buffer.

visualExplanation.reason: Diverging plotted trajectories carry central comparison.
visualExplanation.evidence: Final screenshot white steep fall and pink nearly flat curve.

playfulness.reason: Single dose and auto remainder let learner choose pace.
playfulness.evidence: Both controls exercised; reset not exercised.

practicalValue.reason: Blood example names relevance without concrete action.

depth.reason: Dose response, early sharp change and acid/base inventory ratio connected.
depth.evidence: First/final dose and reveal inventory explanation.

complexity.reason: Core explanation links logarithmic pH, hydrogen ions, acid/base conversion, mol quantities and ratio.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Multiple unfamiliar dependent abstractions despite supported chart.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Moderate: dense prompt and clipped initial readouts.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: high: pH, mol, acetate and acetic acid
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: high: decimal mol, mol/L, logarithmic scale and paired ratio

whyCool: One acid click drops the water curve four pH units while the buffer barely moves, then the reveal connects resistance to disappearing acetate.
caveat: No capacity-exhaustion boundary is available in tested ten-dose path; initial badges clip and fresh transfer was not tested.
